title: Vulnerability Types and Attack Surfaces

header.html: 2.4 Explain types of vulnerabilities and attack surfaces
the official CompTIA Security+ SY0-801 V8 exam objectives, document version 2.0

html:
1Groups of vulnerabilities

Group Vulnerabilities
Products and systems Unsupported products, unpatched systems, obsolete systems, unmanaged systems
Exposure Ports and services left open, shadow IT, rogue devices
Software and code Applications, code, operating system (OS)-based, virtualization, zero-day, cryptographic vulnerabilities
Configuration and data Misconfiguration, public repositories, public object storage
Identity Unmanaged or stale credentials, identity providers
Devices and communication Mobile devices, wireless and low-powered communications
New in V8 Large language models (LLMs) as a surface

2Product and system weaknesses

Weakness Why it is dangerous Fix
Unsupported product The vendor no longer issues patches (end of life) Replace or isolate
Unpatched system A known fix has not been applied Patch management
Obsolete system Old design, cannot meet modern controls Retire, replace or compensate
Unmanaged system Not in inventory, no updates or monitoring Asset inventory, enrollment
Open ports and services Unneeded listening services widen the surface Close or disable; hardening
Shadow IT Tools and cloud services used without IT approval Discovery, policy, approved alternatives
Rogue device An unauthorized device on the network Network access control, scanning
Exam tip

. Zero-day = the flaw is unknown to the vendor and has no patch. End-of-life software is unsupported. A device nobody tracks is unmanaged. Fix the surface by removing what is not needed.

3Application and code vulnerabilities

Item Meaning
Race condition The result depends on timing of events; time-of-check (TOC) to time-of-use (TOU) flaws let data change between the check and the use
Malicious update An update that contains malware
Hardcoded secrets Passwords or keys written in source code
Unsafe exception handling Errors that reveal information or leave the system in an insecure state
OS-based Flaws in the operating system itself
Virtualization VM escape, hypervisor flaws, VM sprawl
Cryptographic vulnerabilities Weak algorithms, short keys, bad key management
Exam tip

. Fix a vulnerability by removing the cause: patch or replace unsupported software, close unused ports, review stale credentials.

4Configuration, data and identity exposure

Item Meaning
Misconfiguration Wrong settings, such as default passwords or open permissions
Public repositories Code repositories that expose secrets (keys, tokens)
Public object storage Cloud storage buckets open to everyone
Unmanaged or stale credentials Old accounts, shared passwords and service accounts nobody reviews
Identity providers A weakness at the IdP can affect every connected application
Mobile devices Loss, theft, jailbreaking, unmanaged apps
Wireless and low-powered communications Weak encryption, interception, and devices with little built-in security
LLMs Prompt injection, data leaks and unsafe output (module 8)
Exam tip

. Hardcoded secrets in a public repository are a common cause of cloud breaches. An open object storage bucket is a misconfiguration. Stale accounts are found by access reviews.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors discovers that a developer committed a cloud access key to a public code repository. Which vulnerabilities does this show?

  • AA race condition in the kernel
  • BAn obsolete operating system
  • CAn unmanaged mobile device
  • DHardcoded secrets exposed in a public repository
Show the answer

Answer: D. Secrets stored in code and published in a public repository are exposed for anyone to use.

S2A vendor announces that a server product will no longer receive security updates. How is this product described?

  • AUnsupported
  • BZero-day
  • CShadow IT
  • DRogue
Show the answer

Answer: A. A product that no longer gets patches is unsupported (end of life).

S3A flaw is being exploited, and the vendor has not yet released a patch because it was unaware. What is this?

  • AA misconfiguration
  • BA zero-day vulnerability
  • CA stale credential
  • DA cryptographic downgrade
Show the answer

Answer: B. A flaw unknown to the vendor with no patch available is a zero-day.

S4A team uses an unapproved file-sharing service to exchange customer data. Which term fits?

  • AShadow IT
  • BRogue device
  • CTime-of-use flaw
  • DObsolete system
Show the answer

Answer: A. Technology used without the approval or knowledge of IT is shadow IT.

S5A check confirms a file's permissions and then a different file replaces it before the file is opened. Which flaw is this?

  • ABuffer overflow
  • BPrivilege creep
  • CTime-of-check to time-of-use race condition
  • DUnsafe exception handling
Show the answer

Answer: C. The state changed between the check and the use, a classic TOC/TOU race condition.

S6Which action best reduces the exposure from unneeded open ports and services on a server?

  • ADisable the services that are not required
  • BAdd more user accounts
  • CIncrease the log retention
  • DInstall a second antivirus
Show the answer

Answer: A. Removing unneeded listening services shrinks the attack surface.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What is a zero-day vulnerability?

Show the answer

A flaw unknown to the vendor with no patch yet.

R2What does TOC/TOU stand for?

Show the answer

Time-of-check and time-of-use, a race condition.

R3What is shadow IT?

Show the answer

Technology used without IT approval.

R4Give two examples of misconfiguration.

Show the answer

Default passwords and public object storage.

R5What is a rogue device?

Show the answer

An unauthorized device connected to the network.

R6Why are stale credentials risky?

Show the answer

Old or unused accounts can be abused and nobody notices.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Systems unsupported, unpatched, obsolete, unmanaged; open ports and services; shadow IT; rogue devices
Code race conditions (TOC/TOU), malicious update, hardcoded secrets, unsafe exceptions, OS flaws, virtualization, weak cryptography, zero-day
Exposure misconfiguration, public repositories, public object storage, stale credentials, identity providers, mobile and wireless, LLMs
